title: Trauma secondary survey

guidelineVersions: NICE NG39, Major trauma: assessment and initial management (2016)
NICE NG37, Fractures (complex): assessment and management (2016)
NICE NG41, Spinal injury: assessment and initial management (2016)

brief.scenario: You are the core surgical trainee in the major trauma receiving area. A 32-year-old conscious cyclist was struck by a car. The trauma team has completed a primary survey and initial resuscitation. The patient is haemodynamically stable, with a pelvic binder in place for suspected pelvic injury and spinal precautions maintained.
brief.task: Perform and describe a safe structured secondary survey to the examiner and present immediate priorities. Nine minutes.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: A systematic head-to-toe reassessment after, never instead of, primary-survey resuscitation.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Routine log-roll in a patient with a suspected pelvic fracture before pelvic imaging.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Confirm primary-survey stability and team handover, protect spine and binder, obtain analgesia and begin structured head-to-toe assessment.

flow: Confirm CABCDE completed; review vitals, mechanism, interventions and analgesia.
Head/face, neck/spine, chest and abdomen: inspect and palpate safely, checking neurological symptoms.
Pelvis/perineum, limbs, distal neurovascular function and exposed surfaces without unsafe movement.
Integrate findings, identify imaging and reassessment needs with trauma leader.
Document injuries and negative findings, arrange tertiary survey and communicate deterioration triggers.

grid.label: Entry safety and handover
grid.borderline: Asks whether primary survey done but does not verify physiology.
grid.pass: Confirms current ABCDE stability and handover.
grid.high: Prioritises repeat CABCDE if any new deterioration.

grid.label: Mechanism and history
grid.fail: Takes no mechanism or risk history.
grid.pass: Uses AMPLE, timing and mechanism with targeted symptoms.
grid.high: Identifies distracting injuries and limitations of the current examination.

grid.label: Head and neck
grid.fail: Moves neck or omits neurological assessment.
grid.pass: Assesses scalp, face, pupils, cervical tenderness and neurology with spinal protection.
grid.high: Plans imaging and repeated neurological observations where indicated.

grid.label: Chest and abdomen
grid.pass: Examines chest wall, breathing, abdomen and back-related symptoms within safe movement limits.
grid.high: Links findings to occult thoracoabdominal injury and need for imaging.

grid.label: Pelvis and perineum
grid.fail: Repeatedly springs pelvis or loosens binder.
grid.borderline: Notes binder but does not assess bleeding signs.
grid.pass: Leaves binder in place; checks perineal/urethral injury signs without destabilisation.
grid.high: Uses NG37 pelvic imaging guidance and avoids routine log roll.

grid.label: Limbs and vascular
grid.fail: Misses an injured limb or distal perfusion.
grid.pass: Examines four limbs, wounds, pulses, capillary refill, movement and sensation.
grid.high: Anticipates occult injury and documents repeat distal neurovascular checks.

grid.label: Safe posterior examination
grid.fail: Log rolls routinely before pelvic imaging.
grid.borderline: Recognises need to check back but gives no safe plan.
grid.pass: Defers log roll in suspected pelvic fracture pending imaging unless a specific exception applies.
grid.high: Explains exceptional airway/penetrating wound indications and controls spinal alignment.

grid.label: Investigation and reassessment
grid.fail: Orders imaging but omits clinical reassessment.
grid.pass: Discusses CT strategy with trauma leader and repeats observations; deteriorating patient returns to primary survey.
grid.high: Uses appropriate whole-body CT in stable adult with blunt major trauma and suspected multiple injuries.

grid.label: Handover and tertiary survey
grid.pass: Documents positives/negatives, announces priorities, plans tertiary survey.
grid.high: Hands over uncertain findings and monitoring triggers explicitly.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: You said the primary survey is finished, so I will get started immediately.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will turn your head to inspect both sides of your neck.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The patient is wearing spinal precautions.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: They can come off while I check it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The abdomen looks all right. I will skip a full chest examination.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: There is a pelvic binder in place.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will remove the binder and spring the pelvis to see if it is stable.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: We should log roll now with two nurses even though pelvic imaging is not done.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The leg is obviously broken so there is no reason to check distal pulses or sensation.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Now BP drops to 86 systolic and pulse rises to 132.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I want to complete my head-to-toe assessment before calling the trauma leader.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Just “secondary survey normal apart from leg fracture”.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I am the core surgical trainee. I will confirm that the primary survey and initial resuscitation have been completed and the patient remains stable before starting a secondary survey.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The team has completed it; the patient is stable.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Please can I have current observations and confirm spinal precautions and the pelvic binder remain in place?

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: HR 102, BP 122/78, RR 20, SpO₂ 97% on air, GCS 15; precautions maintained.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Can you tell me what happened, and whether you lost consciousness?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: A car hit my bicycle. I did not black out. My right leg hurts.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Any medicines, allergies, previous problems, or when you last ate?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: No regular medicines or allergies. I last ate about three hours ago.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will assess scalp and face while maintaining spinal protection, check pupils and ask about neck pain, tingling or weakness.

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: No tingling or weakness.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Small scalp abrasion, no unstable facial injury; pupils equal.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will examine respiratory effort, chest wall and breath sounds and then inspect and gently palpate the abdomen.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Mild right chest-wall tenderness; normal effort, soft abdomen with mild lower tenderness.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will not spring the pelvis or remove the binder. I will inspect safely for perineal bleeding or signs of urethral injury.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: No bleeding seen; binder remains in place.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will examine all four limbs and document deformity, wounds and distal circulation, sensation and movement.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Right lower-leg deformity; foot warm, DP pulse present, sensation and movement intact.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Shall we log roll to inspect the back now?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Not routinely before pelvic imaging in suspected pelvic fracture. I would only do so for an exception such as urgent airway clearance or an occult penetrating injury with instability, with the trauma team protecting alignment.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: With the trauma leader I would request appropriate CT, including whole-body CT if adult blunt major trauma with suspected multiple injuries, and continue repeated observations.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: BP now falls to 86 systolic; pulse 132.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would stop the secondary survey, call the trauma leader immediately and restart CABCDE, seeking and controlling major haemorrhage, while preparing resuscitation and urgent definitive management.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would hand over the documented injury list, key negative findings, binder and spinal status, investigations requested, and arrange a tertiary survey after stabilisation.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I am the core surgical trainee. Before starting, I need confirmation of the trauma leader’s handover, the completed CABCDE and current physiological trend. I will stop and repeat primary assessment if stability changes.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Primary assessment is complete and the patient is initially stable.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Please give me pulse, blood pressure, breathing rate, saturations and GCS. I will keep the binder and spinal protection in place.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Pulse 102, BP 122/78, RR 20, saturations 97% on air, GCS 15.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello. I am checking for injuries that can be missed at first assessment. Is it all right if I ask a few questions and then examine you systematically?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Yes. My right leg is painful.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Were you wearing a helmet? Do you remember the collision or losing consciousness?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: I wore a helmet; I remember it all and did not black out.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Any allergies, medicines including anticoagulants, medical problems, and last meal?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: No medicines or allergies. I ate three hours ago.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will examine the scalp and facial bones while my colleague maintains cervical alignment, check pupils and assess upper and lower limb neurology. Any neck pain, pins and needles or weakness?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: No.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Scalp abrasion; no facial instability; equal pupils.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will inspect the chest for bruising or asymmetry, palpate gently, listen to breathing and examine the abdomen. Please describe any focal findings.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Right chest-wall tenderness, no respiratory compromise; lower abdomen mildly tender, no guarding.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would inspect accessible perineal and genital areas with consent and chaperone as appropriate, looking for bleeding or urethral injury, without springing the pelvis or moving the binder.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: No perineal bleeding visible.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will document all limb wounds and deformity, compare pulses, capillary refill, motor and sensation distally, and repeat the checks after splinting.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Right lower-leg deformity; distal pulse and neurology intact.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Should we log roll now to check the back?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No routine log roll before pelvic imaging when a pelvic fracture is suspected. If the airway cannot otherwise be cleared, or there is suspected occult penetrating injury with instability, the trauma leader may authorise a carefully coordinated roll with haemodynamic monitoring.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will present this injury inventory to the trauma leader. Given adult blunt high-energy trauma and suspected multiple injuries, I would discuss whole-body CT with appropriately directed limb imaging, maintaining observation and readiness to re-enter CABCDE.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The blood pressure is now 86 systolic and pulse 132.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That is a new haemorrhagic shock concern. I will stop secondary examination, announce deterioration, repeat CABCDE, activate major haemorrhage response as indicated and immediately reassess external, thoracic, abdominal and pelvic bleeding with the trauma leader.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: My handover: scalp abrasion, right chest tenderness, lower-abdominal tenderness, pelvic injury suspected with binder in situ, right leg deformity with intact distal neurovascular status. I would record negatives, outstanding scans and a tertiary survey after resuscitation.

failures.move: Continuing secondary examination through new hypotension.
Removing binder or repeatedly springing unstable pelvis.
failures.consequence: May disrupt clot and aggravate bleeding.

failures.move: Routine log roll before imaging in suspected pelvic fracture.
failures.consequence: Potentially destabilises pelvic injury, contrary to NG37.

failures.move: Omitting distal neurovascular examination of deformed leg.
failures.consequence: Misses limb-threatening vascular or neural compromise.

recovery.when: If you started before confirming current stability
recovery.line: I need to confirm current stability and the trauma leader’s primary-survey findings before continuing.

recovery.when: If you were about to log roll with suspected pelvic injury
recovery.line: With suspected pelvic injury I will defer routine log rolling until imaging and stop immediately if physiology deteriorates.

knowledge.fact: NICE NG41 recommends a prioritising sequence such as <C>ABCDE with cervical spine protection, before hospital and again in the emergency department.
NG37 recommends CT as first-line imaging in adults (16 or over) with suspected high-energy pelvic fractures.

NG37: do not log roll people with suspected pelvic fractures before pelvic imaging unless an occult penetrating injury is suspected with haemodynamic instability, or log rolling is needed to clear the airway; when log rolling, watch haemodynamic stability closely.
NG39 supports whole-body CT in adults with blunt major trauma and suspected multiple injuries.
In a newly unstable patient, prioritise resuscitation and primary reassessment; NG39 recommends damage control surgery for haemodynamic instability not responding to volume resuscitation.

recall.think: Secondary survey is conditional on continuing primary-survey stability.
recall.say: “I will check systematically but stop if the patient deteriorates.”
do: Head-to-toe, preserve spine and binder, document distal neurovascular findings.

numbers.meaning: Adult suspected multiple-injury blunt trauma may need whole-body CT; no isolated vital-sign threshold replaces reassessment.

recall.trap: Routine pelvic springing or pre-imaging log roll in suspected pelvic fracture.
recall.finish: Share injury inventory, imaging plan and tertiary-survey handover.

partner.opening: The primary survey has been completed. The patient is stable; proceed with your secondary survey.
partner.actorBrief: Patient says only “My right leg hurts.” If asked, no loss of consciousness, no neck weakness or tingling; helmet worn, no anticoagulants; last meal 3 hours ago.

reveals.trigger: Examiner gives current observations ONLY if requested
reveals.finding: HR 102, BP 122/78, RR 20, SpO₂ 97% air, GCS 15.

reveals.trigger: Exam findings only when region is examined: head and face
Exam findings only when region is examined: chest
reveals.finding: chest mild right-sided tenderness without respiratory distress

reveals.trigger: Exam findings only when region is examined: abdomen
reveals.finding: abdomen soft, mildly tender in lower abdomen

reveals.trigger: Exam findings only when region is examined: pelvis
reveals.finding: pelvis binder applied (do not repeatedly test pelvic stability)

reveals.trigger: Exam findings only when region is examined: limbs
reveals.finding: right lower leg deformity with intact dorsalis pedis pulse, sensation and toe movement.

curveballs.prompt: First curveball at relevant posterior-survey decision: examiner asks “Shall we log roll now?”
curveballs.safeAnswer: Not routinely before pelvic imaging in suspected pelvic fracture. I would only do so for an exception such as urgent airway clearance or an occult penetrating injury with instability, with the trauma team protecting alignment.

curveballs.prompt: Second cue after candidate gives imaging plan: “The blood pressure falls to 86 systolic and pulse rises to 132.”
curveballs.safeAnswer: Candidate must restart CABCDE and mobilise trauma team rather than continue an examination.
